personality_one_liner: A trustworthy, highly legible, and native-feeling mobility app that contrasts a friendly, vibrant passenger experience with a focused, utilitarian driver workflow.

spacing.rule: Generous iOS-native rhythm. Use lg (16pt) for screen padding, md (12pt) between cards, and sticky CTAs with safe area clearance.

do's: Use blur on bottom sheets (Where to? selector).
Use blur on sticky CTAs and sticky headers.
dont's: Avoid blur on individual list rows or dense data cards.

screens.name: AuthAndRole
screens.purpose: A clean onboarding screen asking for Name, Phone Number, and a segmented control to enter as Passenger or Driver.
screens.layout: Hero image at the top with a gradient scrim. Title 'Last-Mile', simple inputs for Name and Phone. A prominent toggle/pill for Role (Passenger/Driver). 'Continue' sticky at the bottom. Driver side uses brandSecondary (charcoal) accents, Passenger uses brandPrimary (emerald).

screens.name: PassengerHome
screens.purpose: Hub-to-hub selection for the passenger and vehicle tier choice.

states.error: Error toast if no hubs available

screens.layout: Abstract background route graphic. A persistent glass bottom sheet takes up the lower half. Inside the sheet: Pick-up Hub dropdown, Drop-off Hub dropdown (using Chennai hubs like Ashok Pillar, SRM, DLF). Below that, a horizontal toggle for '3-Seat Auto' vs '4-Seat Cab'. A sticky primary CTA 'Find Shared Ride' anchored at the bottom.

screens.name: PassengerMatchStatus
screens.purpose: Shows live pooling status, driver match, large PIN, and SOS actions.

states.loading: Full-screen 'Finding riders...' view with animated pulsing avatars and node graphics.

screens.layout: Once matched: Top card shows Driver Avatar, Name, Vehicle Number, and ETA. Middle card is a highly visible 'Ride PIN' block in oversized text. Bottom section shows fare split, shared capacity dots (e.g. 2/3 filled), and sticky bottom buttons for SOS and Share Trip.

screens.name: DriverHome
screens.purpose: Driver dashboard showing Online/Offline status and incoming batch requests.

states.empty: Illustration of auto/cab with 'You are online. Waiting for nearby hub requests.'

screens.layout: Header with 'Go Offline' toggle. Main content is a vertical list of Request Cards. Each card shows: Hub Route (A -> B), Total Passenger Count, Total Fare, and a prominent 'Accept Batch' button. Uses brandSecondary (charcoal) as the primary action color to maintain the utilitarian feel.

screens.name: DriverActiveRide
screens.purpose: Managing the accepted batch, checking PINs, and navigating.
screens.layout: Header shows current destination hub. A list of passenger rows, each with an Avatar, Name, and an input/verify button for their PIN. Large sticky CTA at the bottom to 'Navigate (Opens Maps)' or 'Complete Hub Run' once all passengers are verified/dropped.

instructions_to_main_agent: Build a unified app with a 'AuthAndRole' root screen to toggle between Passenger and Driver flows. This saves creating two separate repositories while achieving the user's goal.

Enforce visual contrast between roles: Use `brandPrimary` (Emerald Green) for all major buttons and active states in the Passenger flow. Use `brandSecondary` (Charcoal) for the Driver flow to make it feel strictly utilitarian.
Map-less routing: Since hubs are fixed, use standard vertical timelines (small circles connected by a vertical dashed line) to visualize routes rather than a Google Map integration.
Implement a polished Bottom Sheet using `@gorhom/bottom-sheet` on the Passenger Home screen.
Passenger Match Status: Ensure the PIN text is rendered large (using 2xl/3xl scaling) so it's instantly readable from a distance.
Remember to include gradient scrims (Layer 1 transparent to Layer 2 70% surfaceInverse) underneath text that sits on top of images (e.g. Auth Hero).
